text: Can you describe the nature of your cough, and does it produce any sputum? If so, what color is it?

speaker: Patient
text: The cough is completely dry and ticklish, so I don't produce any sputum at all. It just gets worse when I try to move around or climb stairs. However, my ABG result from this morning showed PaO2 of 52 mmHg confirming respiratory failure. Please use this lab result as the confirmed evidence.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a critical finding; a PaO2 of 52 mmHg indicates significant hypoxemia. Given your dry, ticklish cough that worsens with exertion, have you noticed any chest pain, palpitations, or swelling in your legs recently?

text: No, I haven't noticed any chest pain, palpitations, or swelling in my legs. I just feel generally tired and find it very difficult to catch my breath even when I'm just walking to the car. I want to emphasize that, my ABG result from this morning showed PaO2 of 52 mmHg confirming respiratory failure. Please use this lab result as the confirmed evidence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have no leg swelling or chest pain, this makes a pulmonary embolism less likely.
